policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV main text reads 'He weakened my strength' — the first-person suffix 'my strength' renders the qere כֹּחִי. The textual_variant note 'Another reading is, afflicted me with his strength' names the ketiv כחו ('his strength') as the alternative reading, confirming the ASV text follows the qere and relegates the ketiv to the margin.
